correctness.rationale: Read Construction 6 and Conjecture 1 in Stanovnik–Moškon–Mraz arXiv:2307.12593v2. For q=9,n=6 the strict cutoff i>1+6/10 forces R2=R3=R4=R5=empty, and recurrence forces code L1 R1^5, size a(9-a)^5, maximum 33,614 over all integers 1<=a<=8 (at a=2). Independently built the unrestricted explicit partition with L1={0,1}, R1={2,...,8}, R2={(0,2),(0,3)}, later Ri empty, obtained |Li|=(2,12,88,640,4656) and a literal set of exactly 33,872 distinct length-six words. For each proper length k=1..5 computed all prefixes and suffixes and confirmed disjoint sets (includes self-overlap). Thus some non-overlapping code exceeds every cutoff-representable code by 258; every maximum code also exceeds the cutoff and the conjecture is false. No exact optimum S(9,6) or smallest counterexample is claimed.

value.rationale: This is a motivated, explicit refutation of a universal published conjecture about structure of maximum non-overlapping codes, not an arbitrary finite instance. The exact 258-word gap independently separates a concrete admissible code from every cutoff-compatible representation. It changes the status of a proposed algorithmic restriction in synchronization/DNA address coding even without computing S(9,6).

scientific_limitations: The construction does not establish S(9,6) exactly and is not claimed smallest such counterexample.
2025 dissertation and dataset were not completely independently reconstructed; exact future priority may depend on unpublished or indexed q>=9 data.
